question: What makes a low-side crash different from a high-side in MotoGP?
answer: A low-side happens when the rear tyre loses grip, so the bike drops to the inside and you slide. A high-side happens when the tyre slides, then suddenly grips again, and the bike flicks you up and over. Rossi says the high-side with the gas closed throws you higher and harder.
move: Low-side: grip goes and you slide. High-side: grip comes back and you fly.

web.label: Flip between two MotoGP crash sequences and watch the rear tyre: one where grip is lost and the bike slides out to the inside, and one where grip returns and the rider is flicked up and over. Asks what makes a low-side crash different from a high-side.
